crypto_published_justification: Every complete example requires ESPHome native API Noise encryption. The pinned ESPHome implementation uses Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256 through its FLOSS crypto library with a256-bit PSK; Xiaomi decryption uses the built-in AES128-CCM component. No project cipher or custom cryptographic algorithm is implemented. Plaintext MQTT/BLE boundaries are explicit. https://github.com/4alvit/esphome-ble-sensor-patterns/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_pfs_justification: Interactive API transport uses Noise NNpsk0 with ephemeral Curve25519 exchange. Passive sensor advertisements are not forward-secret transport; local MQTT must be confined or separately secured with TLS. https://github.com/4alvit/esphome-ble-sensor-patterns/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project has no user-password database. API PSKs, sensor bindkeys and upstream Wi-Fi/MQTT credentials are operator secrets, not user password verifiers. Plaintext password-based OTA/web authentication is not enabled. https://github.com/4alvit/esphome-ble-sensor-patterns/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_random_justification: Operators generate unique API keys with openssl rand -base64 32. Pinned ESPHome Noise code gets handshake randomness from esphome::random_bytes backed by the ESP32 hardware RNG and fails if it is unavailable. Synthetic CI keys are explicitly forbidden for deployment. https://github.com/4alvit/esphome-ble-sensor-patterns/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Native parser tests use active C++ assertions; the Python tests run without optimization disabling assertions. https://github.com/4alvit/esphome-ble-sensor-patterns/blob/main/tests/inkbird_native.cpp
